This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum
 Oral Judgment
(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum) This appeal is by the claimants
who are major sons questioning the quantum as well as negligence on account Nc:
2024:Khc-K:9807 of death of their mother Kamalabai in the road traffic accident dated 15.4.2012.
2. The Tribunal in absence of income proof assessed the income at Rs.4,000/- and awarded Rs.4,68,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.
Tribunal in all awarded Rs.5,18,000/- with interest at 9% per annum.

3. The Tribunal referring to the charge sheet materials apportioned negligence in the ratio of 30:70 i.e. 70% negligence was attributed to the driver of the goods truck bearing No.MH-13-AX 2339 and 30% to the driver of the offending truck bearing No.KA 36-A-2976 who had illegally parked the truck in the middle of the road.

sentences.text: The Tribunal having apportioned the negligence dismissed the claim petition against respondent No.4/New India Insurance company on the ground it is not liable to pay 70% of compensation since the inmates of the goods vehicle were traveling as gratuitous passengers.

The claim petition was in fact allowed against the owner of the NC: 2024:KHC-K:9807 offending truck i.e. respondent No.3 and 30% liability was fastened on respondents 1 and 2 primarily fixing the liability on respondent No.2/Oriental Insurance Company Limited.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants /claimants and the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2/Oriental Insurance Company as well as the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.4/New India Assurance Company limited.
FINDING ON NEGLIGENCE:

6. This Court in MFA.No.202567/2019 considering the arguments advanced by the counsel appearing for the claimants and the counsel appearing for both the Insurance Companies has after meticulous examination of the material on record and on an elaborate discussion held that both the drivers of the truck were negligent and therefore, attributed negligence in the ratio of 50:50.
Accordingly, negligence is attributed in the ratio of 50:50 on the drivers of both the vehicles involved in the NC: 2024:KHC-K:9807 accident.

Further more, since the truck bearing No. MH- 13-AX-2339 was used in violation of the policy conditions permitting 30 passengers to travel in the goods vehicle, Respondent No.3, who is the owner of the truck bearing No. MH-13-AX-2339 is liable to deposit 50% of the compensation awarded.

Respondent No.2/Insurance Company who is the insurer of the goods vehicle bearing No. KA.36/A.2976 which was illegally parked is jointly and severally liable along with respondent No.1 to deposit 50% of the compensation awarded.

FINDING ON QUANTUM:
7.
In the case on hand, the sons are before this Court seeking enhancement.
On independent review of the material on record, this Court of the view that the income assessed at Rs.4,000/- is on the lower side.
In the absence of income proof, this Court is inclined to refer to the income chart of the legal services authority wherein the notional income is prescribed at Rs.6,500/- per month.
However, the claimants in the case on hand, have NC: 2024:KHC-K:9807 specifically pleaded that deceased was earning Rs.6,000/- per month.

Accepting the same, income is assessed at Rs.6,000/-
per month.
If 25% is added towards future prospects, it works out to Rs.7,500/-.

After deducting 1/3rd towards personal expenses, the income works out to Rs.5,000/- and applying the multiplier 13, compensation payable under the head of loss of dependency is determined at (Rs.5,000x12x13)=Rs.7,80,000/-.
8.
Three sons have filed the claim petition.
Therefore, under conventional heads, Rs.1,50,000/- is awarded.

Additionally, 10% escalation for every three years is awarded on the conventional heads applying the principles laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs.
Pranay Sethi and Ors1.

sentences.text: Accordingly, Rs.30,000/- additional amount is added under the conventional heads.
Hence, the total compensation re-determined by this Court works out Rs.9,60,000/- as against Rs.5,18,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Thus, the enhanced compensation Arjun vs Mohammed Hanif on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15227196/
3 works out to 2017 ACJ 2700 SC NC: 2024:KHC-K:9807 Rs.4,42,000/-, which the appellants are held entitled with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

9. For the foregoing reasons, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 19.12.2018 passed by the Tribunal in MVC.No.929/2012 is hereby modified.

(iii) The appellants/claimants are held entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.4,42,000/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
(iv) The negligence is fixed in the ratio of 50:50 on the drivers of both the vehicles.

Respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally held liable to deposit 50% of compensation awarded and balance 50%
shall be paid by respondent No.3/Owner of the offending vehicle i.e. MH-13-AX-2339.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:9807 (v) The order of the Tribunal insofar as apportionment remains unaltered.
